newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares fall, bank stocks dominate.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares fall, bank stocks dominate.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell 0.21 percent on Monday in quiet trade dominated by banking shares.

The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index slipped 0.33 points to close at 153.27 points after shares worth 470,000 dinars ($664,000) changed hands. Trade in Arab Bank, The Housing Bank and Bank of Jordan accounted for more than half that turnover.
"There's a lot of interest in Arab Bank before its AGM on Friday," said analyst Mohammad Abdullah.

The stock fell back 1.25 dinars to close at 254.25 dinars after trade worth nearly 150,000 dinars. Arab Bank has had to put on hold plans for a bonus share issue since the government tied cancellation of a 15 percent tax on capital increases to passage of a parliamentary law covering the Amman bourse.
The Housing Bank, which is to be formally converted into a commercial bank, rose 0.09 dinars to 4.89 while Bank of Jordan closed unchanged on 2.80 dinars.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 19 to seven, with another 14 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange fell 0.24 percent 80.56 points, 3.40 percent down from the start of the year.
